KE.name: Knight Emperor
KE.desc: Knight of Elrios, forging his own path. As the poster boy of the game, KE is a straightforward and well-rounded Physical Main DPS with some impactful utility skills and simple rotation. To bring out his full potential, characters who are able to debuff him such as Code: Antithese and Overmind become are very nice to have, but he's a well-valued addition to Phys comps nonetheless.
KE.pros: Great bossing and clearing tools, provides party-wide super armor and debuffing, relatively simple to play.
KE.cons: Skills have slow casts, limited movement flexibility.

RM.name: Rune Master
RM.desc: A magic swordsman who wields fiery runes. Leaning into his affinity for casting fire spells, RM is a standard Magical Sub DPS who can be great in the right hands. He's slightly outshined by his brothers and the absolute monsters that are Twins Picaro and Morpheus, as well as having some awkward utility that doesn't seem to really shine in any particular content, but provides more party-wide benefits than the aforementioned two for comps in need of some flexibility.
RM.cons: Very average output and a master of no trades

IM.name: Immortal
IM.desc: A swordsman with endless potential. By accepting the power of the Dark El and taking up the blade Conwell, IM is a Physical Main DPS whose main schtick is summoning an infinite number of swords. While a bit less comfortable to play than his other Physical counterpart, his damage floor and ceiling are notably much higher, whose skills have much faster cast times to boot. However, the trade-off is that he offers much lower utility as a result, making him a less popular pick in parties unless players prove themselves as capable pilots.
IM.cons: Subpar clearing, not great for beginners,

GN.name: Genesis
GN.desc: Guardian of Elrios. Sacrificing himself to restore the fragmented El, GN loses his humanity and is reborn as the vessel of its will. As the shiny new fourth path, the design of this job is noticably much more modernized than the other Elboys with his larger repository of solutions and improved mobility (including a double jump!). In that sense, he's the easiest out of the four to play, but nevertheless suffers from the same problem of offering not much more than damage.
GN.pros: Very comfortable to play, a playstyle that can keep up with newer characters
GN.cons: Another generic DPS, may need some positioning

AES.name: Aether Sage
AES.desc: An accomplished scholar in the elements. Ever since her last rework, AeS has become an incredibly formidable Magical Main DPS with much needed improvements to her skill rotation. While all Aishas will present some sort of learning curve to most players, AeS is so good such problems become quite negligible in today's endgame meta. This doesn't mean you can just faceroll your keyboard and hope for the best due to her elemental system, but AeS is a very rewarding character to play for the committed.
AES.cons: Needs a dedicated pilot, Only one useful raid buff

OZ.name: Oz Sorcerer
OZ.desc: A witch with a practiced mastery over dark magic. After signing her new contract with the Demon God Angkor, OZ is a Magical Sub DPS who sits a bit closer to the 'outdated' part of the meta, being neither here nor there in terms of her damage output or supporting capabilities. Her main DPS skill, Abysmal Field, is also lingering skill attached to her that make disengaging bosses for mechanics a bit annoying and hurts her contribution to parties. Still, she remains a perfectly viable choice with the right investment and mindset.
OZ.pros: Provides alright utility, Looks really cool
OZ.cons: Suffers from the same problems all the other Aishas do, but with not nearly enough boons to make up for her shortcomings.

MTM.name: Metamorphy
MTM.desc: A powerful magical girl, distorting Time and Space. Drawing from the power of the Moon El, MtM is a very valuable Physical Sub/Main DPS who has gradually become better and better in recent times after a long history of undeserved nerfs (good for her!). Now, not only are her skills much more comfortable to use overall with improved output, she also offers much needed cdr to most Phys comps where sources of it can be quite sparse.
MTM.cons: One of the few jobs who need their 2nd Hyperactive, needs some extra investment to truly feel good to play

LA.name: Lord Azoth
LA.desc: The immortal alchemist, severing ties with her mortality. It's truly a wonder that both Physical Aishas are in such good spots; whereas MtM leans on offering more personal damage, LA offers a wider breadth of amp and utility options. While also not a dedicated support, players seeking to invest in the other Aishas may want to start as LA to be more easily accepted into parties. For those who simply want to main LA, she's sure to deliver from beginning to the end.
LA.pros: Some great contributions without sacrificing damage
LA.cons: Relies slightly on potion RNG, Not remotely a 'true' support so expect to do damage

AN.name: Anemos
AN.desc: A martial artist as swift as the wind. Growing closer with the wind spirits, AN is an incredibly mobile Physical Main DPS with many answers to a variety of encounter problems, being perhaps the character with the most mid-air options. With a fairly simple rotation focused on 2 buttons that each lower the other's cooldown and incredible clearing, she's a versatile and simple option for players who want something easy yet satisfying to play or as a farming option.
AN.pros: Amazing mobility and clearing, Great MP self-sustain
AN.cons: Only offers as much as any other DPS, Not high enough of a damage ceiling

DAB.name: Daybreaker
DAB.desc: The elven representative, breaking the dawn. Long gone are the days of picking one's nose and holding 'Ace in the Hole' with DaB, who has joined the recent meta of spamming immediate and flashy skills, making her a little less unique than previously. However, the change was certainly necessary, as her performance has largely improved since with respect to the current trend of larger and increasingly mobile bosses. Surprisingly, her amp is also quite good for a Magical Main DPS of her calibre, making her a comfortable choice for those who enjoy the standard archer archetype.
DAB.pros: Very easy to play with minimal party requirements, Has some nice amp
DAB.cons: Still not a beginner's best option as per DPS law, Timing skills to ensure they don't miss or result in fatal animation locks may be a hurdle

TW.name: Twilight
TW.desc: Watcher of the night, hidden amongst the forest's shadows. As the representative of Eldrasil's will, TW is an incredible Physical Main DPS with the highest damage ceiling out of all the Renas thanks to her extremely fast-casting skills and mobility. However, and importantly, her main drawbacks are her large consumption of MP (even with a party) and excessively long cooldowns, making her the type of character you'd only want to build around 500 El Resonance levels later. Her reliance on other party members and heavy investment make her somewhat of an unpopular/luxury pick, but will be rewarding for the dedicated.
TW.cons: Chronic MP chugger, Long cooldowns, Has a pretty great debuff but its duration is very awkward to work with

PR.name: Prophetess
PR.desc: Prophet, translator, and bard, transcribing the voices of the world. Through powers of song, PR is an exceptionally excellent Magical Synergy DPS who provides almost every single relevant offensive buff in the game and does it without sacrificing her damage. Despite this, she struggles with long cooldowns and so cdr/cda passives are a must, and is also much more rotationally heavy than most requiring some memorization on the pilot's part.
PR.pros: Incredible raidwide buffs for Mag comps, Support skills tied to damage
PR.cons: Has a learning curve as the order of skills pressed matters, Needs cooldown reduction/acceleration

FB.name: Furious Blade
FB.desc: A swordsman reborn, leaving behind his Nasod body. Although not quite as good as in the past, FB is a perfectly passable Physical Main DPS character with some silly tools in his arsenal for both clearing and bossing. Having said this, he suffers from the classic problem of being overly dependent on continuous sources of MP and cdr/cda, thus requiring a heavier level of investment than most other DPS. His skills, buffs, and hitboxes also need extra attention from the pilot to bring out his full potential.
FB.cons: Minimal utility, High reliance on party members, Awkward skill hitboxes

RH.name: Rage Hearts
RH.desc: Wielding the full power of his Nasod hand, a destructive fighter with explosive capabilities. RH is a somewhat rarely seen but powerful bosser with skills that inflict nearly all of their damage instantaneously. The utility he provides as another Magical Main Dps leave much to be desired, but with a great pilot, can be made up for in pure damage.
RH.pros: Quick and powerful bursts of boss damage
RH.cons: Minimal utility, Doesn't offer much else

NI.name: Nova Imperator
NI.desc: An airship tactician, igniting the path to victory. NI is an excellent Magical Sub DPS with higher than average amp for his role and an emphasis on big-bossing. On the contrary, his small-bossing is much poorer due to less options and slow casts. Thanks to Master of Warfare, he doesn't suffer from MP issues but prefers to stay at lower HP values as a trade-off due to how Overheat works, which might be a hurdle for some.
NI.pros: Nice amp, Has self-sustain, Exceptional big bossing
NI.cons: Slow skill casting, Forcibly lowers own HP to work, Struggles with small bosses

RV.name: Revenant
RV.desc: A wraith knight walking the path of revenge. Consumed by the venom of the mutated Alterasia, RV is possibly currently one of the best, if not the best, Physical Synergy DPS ampers out there; all while also doing great damage at the same time. It's not hard to do well with him; he has a number of ways to weaken enemy defenses and even a button to reset the entire party's cooldowns every 30-seconds, meaning as long as buttons are being pressed, the party immediately benefits, making him the best choice for Raven mains who are just starting out.
RV.pros: Extremely straightforward to play, Incredible support without sacrificing damage, Gets double jump
RV.cons: Suffers from MP/cooldown issues, May be sort of boring to play

CU.name: Code Ultimate
CU.desc: Queen of Destruction, an expert in warfare. As a truly realized battle Nasod, CU isn't the easiest character to play but has much to offer thanks to recent balance patches. While her clearing is still far from the leagues of other Magical Main DPS, not only is Junk Break is a powerful bossing tool, but she also offers some nice amp to the party as well. The Magical DPS pool is over-saturated with incredible damage dealers and supporters, but CU is able to carve out for herself a small place within the meta for those willing to learn her.
CU.cons: Lots of learning curves and can be a bit of an acquired taste

CES.name: Code Esencia
CES.desc: Benevolent Empress of Nasods, finally believing in her humanity. Her main gimmick is to summon her servants Oberon and Ophelia to provide party-wide effects. Though these benefits have taken quite a hit in recent times, CEs is still a nice character to have in Phys comps when all other necessary requirements have been filled. The splash damage from Heaven's Fist is an incredible tool for clearing out entire rooms, and she also offers minimal, but nevertheless not insignificant amp/utility.
CES.pros: Nice supporting capabilities, Fast skills, Great clear
CES.cons: Overshadowed by Antithese, Summons can be a bit annoying, Lacking small boss options

CS.name: Code Sariel
CS.desc: An electric angel that has casted aside her emotions for the battlefield. A phenomenal room clearer through the use of wide-reaching lasers, but only when her gear is strong enough to actually kill. On the bossing side of things, she provides a fair bit of notable amplification but is lacking in the damage department in an otherwise incredibly powerful Magical Main DPS scene, making her somewhat sorely in need of bigger buffs to stay relevant without higher levels of investment.
CS.pros: Great amp, Better mobility than the first two Eves
CS.cons: Provides nothing but amp, overshadowed by other Mag DPS, Can be annoying to play if not over-geared

CA.name: Code Antithese
CA.desc: Queen of Extinction, denying all those who oppose her. Like a true tyrant, CA is an phenomenal Physical Main DPS who is also a shadow of her past (for better or worse) due to a series of nerfs throughout time. Still, she does away with almost everything that tends to make Eve a character that's a bit harder to play than most, focusing on lingering damage skills that flood entire screens. While she offers some utility, her true potential lies in her ability to dish out crazy numbers.
CA.pros: Extremely mobile and easy to control, Versatile DPS skillbars, Has very big numbers
CA.cons: Maybe too powerful, One of the few character who want their Master Skill

CC.name: Comet Crusader
CC.desc: With iron will, a true guardian of justice. Being the classic 'tank' of the game, CC is a utility pick that provides a variety of mostly defensive, and a couple of offensive effects to the party. Wonder Wall is an absolutely bonkers shield that absorbs 50% of damage and grants super armor for 11.5 seconds, assuming it doesn't break before then. He can also dish out some nice damage, but in content where his utility isn't as needed due to more options for survival, he can quickly become rather obsolete.
CC.pros: Defensive abilities that can trivialize a lot of scary content,
CC.cons: Falls off rapidly with large bosses, doesn't provide much other than defense

CENT.name: Centurion
CENT.desc: More of a team player than FP

DA.name: Dius Aer
DA.desc: Phenomenal Physical Support with incredible clearing through Shine Chase.

ETW.name: Eternity Winner
ETW.cons: Reliance on active commands can be a learning curve

RAS.name: Radiant Soul
RAS.desc: Well-rounded and easy to learn healer.
RAS.pros: Longest freeze and great supporting capabilities, not hard to learn.
RAS.cons: Skill casting can be a bit slow

NL.name: Nisha Labyrinth
NL.desc: A devoted savior just for Laby.
